patient_history: Patient is a 7-year-old boy brought in by his mother due to a 2-day history of fever, sore throat, and difficulty swallowing. On examination, tonsils were enlarged and erythematous with white exudate, and tender anterior cervical lymphadenopathy was noted. Rapid strep test was positive. He was diagnosed with streptococcal pharyngitis and prescribed a 10-day course of amoxicillin, with instructions for symptomatic care and follow-up if symptoms worsen.
reference_summary: 7-year-old boy with fever, sore throat, and tonsillar exudate tested positive for strep throat; diagnosed with streptococcal pharyngitis and started on a 10-day amoxicillin course.

patient_history: A 61-year-old female with a history of osteoarthritis presents with progressively worsening right knee pain over six months, worse with activity and improved with rest, without associated swelling, redness, or fever. X-ray of the knee revealed joint space narrowing and osteophyte formation consistent with moderate osteoarthritis. She was advised on weight management, physical therapy, and started on acetaminophen with a plan to consider NSAIDs if inadequate relief.
reference_summary: 61-year-old female with knee osteoarthritis confirmed by X-ray findings of joint space narrowing and osteophytes; managed conservatively with physical therapy and acetaminophen.

patient_history: Patient is a 33-year-old male with no significant past medical history presenting after a motor vehicle accident with complaints of neck pain and headache. He was the restrained driver in a rear-end collision. There is no loss of consciousness reported. Cervical spine X-ray was unremarkable, and CT head showed no acute intracranial abnormality. He was diagnosed with cervical strain and discharged with NSAIDs, a soft cervical collar for comfort, and instructions to follow up if symptoms worsen.
reference_summary: 33-year-old male involved in a rear-end motor vehicle accident presented with neck pain and headache; imaging was unremarkable, and he was diagnosed with cervical strain and discharged with conservative treatment.

patient_history: A 72-year-old female with a history of atrial fibrillation on anticoagulation therapy presents with sudden onset right-sided weakness and slurred speech that began one hour prior to arrival. NIH Stroke Scale score was 12. CT head showed no hemorrhage. She was within the window for thrombolytic therapy and was given intravenous tPA after ruling out contraindications, with subsequent admission to the stroke unit for monitoring.
reference_summary: 72-year-old female with atrial fibrillation presented with acute right-sided weakness and slurred speech consistent with ischemic stroke; received IV tPA within the treatment window and was admitted to the stroke unit.

patient_history: A 50-year-old male with a history of chronic alcohol use presents with a 1-week history of progressive abdominal distension, jaundice, and confusion. Family reports increased somnolence over the past two days. Examination revealed scleral icterus, ascites, and asterixis. Laboratory workup showed elevated liver enzymes, elevated ammonia, and low albumin. He was diagnosed with hepatic encephalopathy secondary to decompensated alcoholic liver cirrhosis and started on lactulose with admission for further management.
reference_summary: 50-year-old male with chronic alcohol use presented with jaundice, ascites, and confusion; diagnosed with hepatic encephalopathy from decompensated cirrhosis and started on lactulose with admission for further care.

patient_history: Patient is a 68-year-old male with a known history of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and a 40-pack-year smoking history, presenting with worsening dyspnea, productive cough with yellow sputum, and wheezing over the past week. He denies fever or chest pain. Physical exam revealed diffuse expiratory wheezes and use of accessory muscles. Chest X-ray showed hyperinflated lungs without consolidation. He was diagnosed with a COPD exacerbation and started on bronchodilators, systemic corticosteroids, and antibiotics.
reference_summary: 68-year-old male with COPD and heavy smoking history presented with an acute exacerbation marked by dyspnea and productive cough; treated with bronchodilators, corticosteroids, and antibiotics after ruling out pneumonia on chest X-ray.

patient_history: A 45-year-old female with a history of hypothyroidism presents for a routine follow-up. She reports fatigue and mild weight gain over the past two months despite adherence to levothyroxine therapy. TSH level was found to be elevated at 8.5 mIU/L, above the therapeutic target. Physical examination was unremarkable aside from mild dry skin. The dose of levothyroxine was increased, and follow-up labs were scheduled in six weeks.
reference_summary: 45-year-old female with hypothyroidism reported fatigue and weight gain; elevated TSH prompted an increase in levothyroxine dosage with follow-up labs planned in six weeks.
